subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Dith Pran (1942-2008) was a photojournalist born in Siem Reap, Cambodia.
• He was of Khmer heritage and survived the Cambodian genocide.
• He was the first Cambodian photojournalist to be the subject of a major Hollywood film.
• Early in his career, he worked as an unnamed local assistant to foreign correspondents, such as his initial assignments for The New York Times (1972).
• Later, he became a credited staff photographer, such as his prominent role documented in The Killing Fields (1984).
prompt: The student wants to make and support a generalization about Dith Pran's early career. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: The Killing Fields (1984) was released after Dith Pran had already worked as a journalist, whereas his role as a consultant came later.
choices.B: Dith Pran wasn't even credited as a journalist in some of his early work, such as his initial assignments for The New York Times (1972), where he served as an unnamed local assistant.
choices.C: The Killing Fields and his later memoir both feature Dith Pran, the first Cambodian photojournalist to be the subject of a major Hollywood film.
choices.D: In his early New York Times work (1972), Dith Pran served as an unnamed local assistant to foreign correspondents.

explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it makes and supports a generalization about Dith Pran's early career. The sentence presents a general claim that 'Dith Pran wasn't even credited as a journalist in some of his early work' and supports it with a specific example: 'his initial assignments for The New York Times (1972), where he served as an unnamed local assistant.' This structure of generalization followed by supporting evidence directly accomplishes the stated goal.
